items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He said that if the American Cultural Center really wanted to do something cultural for his country and the people, they should send a couple of American music professors to teach the young students and musicians

ctx.x: A friend of my wife and I, Colette Lacroix, had given Lily the phone number of the director of the most important newspaper in Dakar, called "The Sun". When we were met at the airport by the Director of the Cultural Center, Lily asked him if any report had been printed in the papers about my arrival and the concert. He said that nothing had been printed concerning the matter. So Lily phoned the Director of the 'Sun' newspaper, who seemed to be a nice person to talk with. He said that he had heard me play several…

He said that if the American Cultural Center really wanted to do something cultural for his country and the people, they should send a couple of American music professors to teach the young students and musicians, the different arts of America, and the right approach to the form of jazz that was known in American, and other parts of the continent.

The director of 'The Sun' had come to the rehearsals also with a young musician in his early thirties who was a trumpet player from Ghana. His name was Mackenzie. He knew quite a lot about jazz and was a quiet/nice person. He told me that he had seen the director of the Cultural Center the previous week and told him that this band would be incapable to accompany me. He had offered to form a little group and make them rehears, but they had declined his offer.
